comparison.objective: Plant a seedling by holding it upright while pouring rigid soil clods around it, then release it self-supporting; candidate tunes and locks an industrial shock absorber through guarded test cycles.
comparison.physical_skill: Pr-680 tests bimanual transport, continuous support of an unstable body, tray tipping, and controlled release. The candidate tests tool alignment into a recessed fastener, collar micro-rotation, bounded locking torque, control actuation, and iterative adjustment from dynamic response.
comparison.success_condition: Pr-680 requires the plug within 2 cm of the hole center and 1.5 cm of its floor, seedling within 10°, at least 32 of 45 clods placed, grippers at least 3.5 cm away, and 2 s stability. The candidate instead requires two safe, repeatable impact stops and lock retention. Pr-680 lacks spill, plant-damage, and pouring-force thresholds, but its clearly different stabilization/filling outcome remains established.
comparison.reason: Although both are bimanual and require a stable released result, they test different abilities: concurrent support-and-filling versus tool-mediated calibration of a dynamic mechanical component.
